name: Apache HTTP/2 RCE
tile_line: Only if HTTP/2 is on. Crash PoC public, no RCE code.
tldr: A race in the HTTP/2 module of Apache httpd 2.4.55 to 2.4.70, and in some older distro builds, may let an attacker with no login run code. Red Hat says a reliable exploit was shown; no code for it is public. If HTTP/2 is on, update or turn HTTP/2 off.
summary: A race condition in Apache's HTTP/2 module can corrupt memory and may let an attacker with no login run code. It only matters if HTTP/2 is turned on. Red Hat says a reliable exploit was shown; public proof-of-concept code crashes the server but doesn't run code. Singapore's Cyber Security Agency says it's reportedly exploited, without naming a source; F5 and Horizon3 report no attacks.

affected.label: httpd 2.4.55 – 2.4.70
affected.text: Also standalone mod_h2 2.0.8–2.0.42. Distro packages differ: Ubuntu 22.04's 2.4.52 is affected through a backport, while base RHEL 8 and Ubuntu 18.04 or older aren't. Red Hat JBoss Core Services is affected, including on RHEL 8. Check your distro's advisory, not just the version number.

affected.label: h2 or h2c in Protocols
affected.text: An active `Protocols` line that includes `h2` or `h2c`.

do.label: Upgrade httpd
do.text: To 2.4.71, or your distro's fixed package. Standalone mod_h2 has no fixed release; switch to the built-in module.

slack: Apache HTTP/2 race (CVE-2026-119618): possible unauthenticated RCE in httpd 2.4.55–2.4.70, only if mod_http2 is loaded and h2/h2c is enabled. Red Hat says a reliable exploit was shown; public PoC code only crashes the server. Singapore's CSA says it's reportedly exploited (no source named); F5 and Horizon3 report no attacks; not in KEV. Check: apachectl -M | grep http2. Fix: 2.4.71 or distro package; stopgap: Protocols http/1.1.

sources.title: Red Hat: CVE page, HTTP/2 required
Horizon3: public PoC crashes, no code execution, no attacks confirmed
CSA Singapore AL-2026-164: "reportedly" exploited, no source named

changes.text: Public crash PoC noted (no code execution). Singapore's CSA says reportedly exploited; others report no attacks. JBoss Core Services affected. Safe versions added.
Review: exploit status set to demonstrated (Red Hat), mod_h2 versions, citations fixed.
